What

What Commercial Stump Grinding Involves

Commercial stump grinding is typically multi-stump scope work on business property — office complexes, retail plazas, industrial parks, and multi-family communities. Every job starts with a site walkthrough with the property manager or facilities lead, followed by a line-item written quote with per-stump or per-scope pricing, a scheduled work window (often after-hours or weekend to minimize disruption), full chip cleanup, and B2B invoicing on Net 30/60 terms.

The distinction that matters: commercial scope carries the same administrative footprint as commercial tree removal — certificates of insurance, additional-insured endorsements, before/after photo documentation, and multi-property service contracts. Equipment is scaled to the site: a compact grinder with 36-inch gate access for tight parcels, a full-size track grinder for high-volume work, and chipper-truck haul-off when chip volume demands it. Topsoil backfill is available where finish-grade is part of the scope.

Common Commercial Questions

Commercial Stump Grinding FAQ

Five things NE Ohio facilities and property managers ask before booking.

Does Roubic provide certificates of insurance for commercial stump-grinding accounts?
Yes — full COIs with additional-insured endorsements are available on request, same as our commercial tree removal accounts.
Can stump grinding be scheduled after-hours to minimize disruption?
Yes — after-hours and weekend scheduling is available with no premium for routine work, same as commercial tree removal. Most commercial accounts schedule grinding during early-morning or weekend windows.
How does pricing work for commercial multi-stump jobs?
Per-stump pricing improves at volume. Most commercial multi-stump jobs price out at 30–50% below per-stump residential rates. Specific quotes are scope-driven and delivered line-item.
Does Roubic handle ROW or municipal coordination for commercial work?
Yes. ROW work near commercial parcels is coordinated with city engineering. Roubic handles the workflow including any required mark-out (Ohio Utilities Protection Service / 811).
How deep do you grind, and what happens to the chips?
We grind stumps 6–12 inches below grade. Chips are cleaned up in full — with chipper-truck haul-off on larger-volume jobs — and topsoil backfill is available where finish-grade is part of the scope.
